Prop Chris Coleman, from Garndiffaith, is a Welsh Under-20 international and made his Dragons bow off the bench against the Scarlets at Judgement Day in 2018.

The front row made another appearance as a replacement in Llanelli against Scarlets in January 2019 and his first start against Timisoara Saracens a week later.

Newport-born Coleman is an Academy graduate at Dragons and has become a senior regular over the past two campaigns leading to his 50th appearance against the Scarlets on Judgement Day at the end of the 2022/23 season. Coleman scored his first Dragons try in the home league fixture against Glasgow Warriors in January 2023.

Coleman's impressive form for Dragons during the 24/25 season earnt him a first Wales call-up for the summer tour to Japan.

Chris Coleman is sponsored bySunnybank Nursery

Lewis made 88 appearances for Cardiff having made his debut in 2014 and was part of the Wales Under-20 squad which won a Six Nations Grand Slam in 2016.

He made his senior Wales debut against Tonga in 2017 and has since earned 57 caps for his country and was part of the side which won the Six Nations in 2019.

Utility Back David/Dai Richards is capable of playing anywhere from 12 to full back and is a Dragons Academy product having previously attended Monmouth school.

Richards made his Dragons senior debut in April 2022, before scoring his first try in a breakaway against Zebre in the following season and following it up with an accrobatic finish in the same game.

Richards rejoined the club following am impressive season at Newport RFC, helping them to the Super Rygbi Cymru title in 2024/25.

David Richards is sponnsored by WBC Group -https://westernbuildingconsultants.com/
選手名_カタカナ: デイヴィッド・リチャーズ

Text_Detail:
Former Wales under 20s international Huw Anderson made his Dragons debut in the 2023/24 season against Ulster.

The full-back or wing scored three tries in six appearances for Wales U20s against Scotland, England and New Zealand and is considered one of the most exciting talents in Welsh rugby.

That impressive strike rate continued into the following season with a try in a Man of the Match display in his first start against Newcastle in the European Challenge Cup, a score which won 24/25 try of the season.

Anderson is a product of Caerphilly RFC having also represented Pontypool RFC and signed a new deal to remain at Dragons ahead of the 25/26 season.
